 Dengue Cases in Yucatán More Than Double in 5 Weeks
 By Yucatán Magazine 
 November 10, 2026 November 10, 2026 
 Confirmed dengue cases in Yucatán have more than doubled since late September, and the strain linked to the most serious cases is circulating in the state’s four hot spots.
 Federal health data show confirmed cases rose from 51 on Sept. 28 to 111 as of Nov. 2. Probable cases, meaning people who saw a doctor with dengue symptoms, climbed 26% over the same five weeks, from 1,999 to 2,519.
 October was busier for clinics and labs. On average, 15 people a day sought care for dengue symptoms, and one or two a day tested positive. In September, it was 12 consultations a day and one confirmed case every 29 hours.
 Yucatán now ranks 15th among Mexican states for confirmed cases, up from 17th at the end of September.

 Which strain, and where
 There are four types of dengue virus. Catching a second, different type can raise the risk of severe illness.
 The federal Secretaría de Salud reports that type 2 is circulating in all four municipalities it has flagged as epidemic or alarm zones. Type 2 is associated with the most severe cases, according to Óscar Flores Munguía, an epidemiologist with ISSSTE, the federal workers’ health system. In the other 22 municipalities with cases, including Mérida, types 2 and 3 are both present. Type 3 drove Yucatán’s 2023 epidemic.
 The newest epidemic zone is an unlikely one. The municipality of Quintana Roo, in eastern Yucatán and not to be confused with the neighboring state, logged its first case of the year in late October. With just 1,036 residents, the state’s smallest population, that single non-severe case was enough to push its rate to 92 per 100,000 people.
 Calotmul, also in the east, remains an epidemic zone with three cases. Ticul, in the south, moved from epidemic to alarm status, though its count rose from 21 to 26 in a week. Buctzotz dropped to the second alarm zone with four cases.
 In all, dengue has been confirmed in 26 of Yucatán’s 106 municipalities. Kanasín, Tixcacalcupul, Temozón, Quintana Roo and Tecoh joined the list in October.
 Deaths and the bigger picture
 Yucatán has no confirmed dengue deaths this year. Fourteen people have died with dengue symptoms; in 10 of those cases dengue was ruled out, and four remain under study.
 The current count is also lower than a year ago. At this point in 2025, the state had 162 confirmed cases and two confirmed deaths. In 2023, Yucatán led the country with more than 10,000 confirmed cases.
 Nationally, confirmed cases rose 49% in five weeks, to 9,456, and confirmed deaths reached 33. The Peninsula accounted for nearly a third of the new confirmed cases. The state of Quintana Roo leads the region with 570 cases and is the only Peninsula state with confirmed deaths, at four. Campeche has 73. Regional outlets have tracked the spread since late summer.
 Dengue spreads through the bite of the Aedes aegypti mosquito, which breeds in standing water. Warning signs include persistent vomiting, intense abdominal pain, bleeding and unusual irritability. Nationally, women make up 55% of confirmed cases, and children ages 10 to 14 are the most affected age group.
 Yucatán Magazine has followed earlier dengue waves , along with the fumigation brigades that spray streets and parks during outbreaks.
 Fast Facts
 Confirmed cases in Yucatán, Jan. 1–Nov. 2: 111 (64 non-severe, 46 with warning signs, one severe)
 Probable cases: 2,519
 Municipalities with cases: 26 of 106
 Epidemic zones: Quintana Roo (municipality) and Calotmul
 Alarm zones: Ticul and Buctzotz
 Strains: type 2 in the four hot spots; types 2 and 3 elsewhere, including Mérida
 Confirmed deaths in Yucatán: zero; four deaths under study
 Same week in 2025: 162 confirmed cases
 Empty standing water weekly and use repellent and window screens.
 With reporting from Diario de Yucatán and Por Esto!, with data from Mexico’s Secretaría de Salud
